Through the study of transient performance technology, the maximum ferro resonance time of the developed UHV CVT is 0.14s, and the transient response time does not exceed 0.5 cycles, which is far superior to the technical requirements specified in the UHV standard. Research on voltage equalization technology for capacitor voltage dividers was conducted through simulation and experiments, and two ring structure voltage equalization ring was designed with a radio interference level not exceeding 1000uV. In order to improve the overall seismic resistance level of UHV substations, research on UHV CVT seismic resistance technology was conducted through simulation and testing. The optimized design of UHV CVT passed the 0.4g seismic resistance test.

articleTitle: Research on Measuring Technique of Burst Power in Ad-Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: Addressing the issue of burst power measurement during the production, usage, and maintenance of Ad-Hoc network terminals, this paper employs a burst signal detection algorithm based on correlation distance and measures the burst signal power through frequency domain analysis. To address the problem of false triggering in this algorithm, an improved method is proposed, and experimental verification is completed using GNU Radio. The results indicate that the algorithm can accurately detect burst signals at different center frequencies and carrier-to-noise ratios. After calibration with standard instruments, the error between the power measurement result and the spectrum analyzer measurement result is less than ±1dB.

articleTitle: Vehicle Trajectory Anomaly Detection Method Based on Trajectory Representation and Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: Trajectory anomaly detection is an important technique for identifying abnormal patterns that significantly differ from normal behavior in the trajectory data of moving objects. This paper explores a trajectory anomaly detection method that integrates trajectory representation and clustering algorithms. This research employs LSTM-RNN to represent the GPS trajectory data of urban vehicles, converting variablelength vehicle trajectories into fixed-length vectors. The DBSCAN algorithm is then applied for trajectory clustering, effectively identifying anomalous trajectories. Experimental results demonstrate that our method can accurately extract abnormal patterns from large-scale trajectory data, achieving a silhouette coefficient of 0.336, indicating good clustering performance.

articleTitle: Construction of R-V Characteristic Curves and Finite Element Simulation Analysis of 10kV MOA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: The proposal of “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals” has led to an increase in the total installed capacity of new energy sources, with a corresponding increase in the number of connections to the grid. As a result, users have become more demanding in terms of the reliability of the electricity system. To improve the safety of the power system, it is essential to install arresters in transmission and distribution lines. This paper presents a case study on the 10kV metal oxide arrester (MOA) as a representative example. Firstly, in this paper, the Metal Oxide Varistor (MOV) is divided into four equal parts. The V-A characteristics of each part are measured. The measured data are then compared with the standard data. It is found that the error is small, thus verifying the feasibility of the method. In the meantime, the measured data were fitted according to the existing formulae in order to obtain the complete R-V characteristic curve. The fitting effect was found to be satisfactory. Finally, a three-dimensional model is constructed according to the actual physical structure of the MOA. An electro-thermal simulation of the whole model is carried out in a program based on the finite element analysis method to obtain the temperature and potential distributions under different electrical stresses. The feasibility of the model is verified by comparing the experimental results with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Coordinated Market Design for Peer-to-Peer Renewable Energy and Renewable Energy Certificate Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative decentralized peer-to-peer (P2P) renewable energy (RE) and renewable energy certificate (REC) coordinated trading mechanism. Renewable energy system (RES) owners act as sellers in this market, engaging in contracts with consumers desiring to purchase both RE and REC, contingent on their REC inventory and forecasted RE output. Consumers, in turn, serve as buyers, procuring RE to meet their load requirements and implementing REC and RE to fulfill their RE accommodation needs. The settlement of RE trades is based on the actual RE output, with shortfall compensated by RES owners who purchase equivalent RE in the real-time energy market and REC in the wholesale REC market. We formulate the trading problem utilizing a scenario-based approach and devise a distributed algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with a communication saving strategy for solution of the trading problem. The outcomes demonstrate that the proposed method effectively facilitates RE and REC P2P trading, fostering increased RE integration and meeting consumers' RE accommodation requirements.

articleTitle: Research on the Method of Monitoring Rice Pests Using the Integration of Photoelectric and Piezoelectric Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: In order to achieve real-time and accurate monitoring of the adult insect population density of rice pests in rice fields, based on the analysis of the principles of photoelectric and piezoelectric technology, this article uses photoelectric and piezoelectric technology to count pests separately, and integrates the counting results obtained by the two methods to optimize the experimental research on rice pest monitoring devices. The experimental results show that under laboratory conditions, the accuracy rate of photoelectric counting method for rice stem borer is 94%, and that for rice leaf roller is 96%. The accuracy rate of piezoelectric counting method for rice stem borer is 80%, and that for rice leaf roller is 76%. However, after integrating the counting results, the accuracy rate of photoelectric counting method for rice stem borer is 96%, and that for rice leaf roller is 98%.

articleTitle: Microgrid Hybrid Energy Storage Control Strategy Based on Fuzzy Active Disturbance Rejection Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: Traditional PI control in photovoltaic and storage microgrid systems faces challenges such as complex parameter adjustment, slow response speed, and a cumbersome adjustment process. This study delves into the hybrid energy storage control system to enhance microgrid power stability and decrease DC bus voltage fluctuations. The paper suggests integrating fuzzy control with active disturbance rejection control in a combined model control strategy for supercapacitor and battery. Fuzzy control is utilized to tune the coefficients of the nonlinear feedback error (SEF) and adjust corresponding coefficients and gains in real-time, thereby enhancing the system's anti-interference capabilities and response time. The model is implemented and validated on the MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform. Experimental findings demonstrate that employing Fuzzy-ADRC+PI control leads to notable reductions in bus voltage fluctuations, faster response times, and increased robustness compared to traditional proportional-integral control and traditional active disturbance rejection control.

articleTitle: Evaluation Methods and Techniques for in-Situ Stress Logging in Oil and Gas Reservoirs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: The utilization of advanced log interpretation techniques plays a crucial role in assessing the mechanical characteristics essential to exploit shale gas reserves effectively. Alongside conventional approaches like acoustic logs or resistivity images that are commonly used for this purpose; newer methodologies including nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) logs or fracture monitoring logs have surfaced recently with promising potential to evaluate these properties comprehensively. By integrating these diverse log data sets into our analyses, we are able to conduct a detailed assessment on stress distribution within shale formations along with their rock mechanics parameters; thereby providing a scientific foundation guiding decisions related to horizontal well placement as well as hydraulic fracturing strategies. Real-time monitoring coupled with ongoing evaluations enables timely adjustments to operational parameters ensuring optimal productivity from these reserves. Extensive research efforts have focused on refining stress evaluation techniques specifically tailored for assessing shale formations through log data interpretation while concurrently accumulating valuable field experience leading to progressive enhancements within our theoretical framework. Through amalgamating multiple cutting-edge log interpretation methodologies, we aim at achieving more precise characterization pertaining to mechanical attributes specific to shale formations thus offering dependable insights supporting future oilfield developments.

articleTitle: Research on Navigation and Tracking Method for Fire Extinguishing Robots in Energy Storage Power Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: A study was conducted on the navigation and positioning of fire extinguishing robots in energy storage power plants. Based on the analysis of the robot's motion model, the RTK satellite positioning kit was used for global positioning of the robot, with a positioning accuracy of ± 2cm. Based on the positioning data, a global map and path were constructed. To ensure that the robot can reach the target point with the shortest path, a trajectory tracking algorithm was designed using LQR optimal control, The feasibility of the algorithm was verified through MATLAB simulation. Experimental tests have shown that the navigation and trajectory tracking controller designed in this paper has the advantages of fast response and high stability, which can meet the motion control requirements of the fire extinguishing robot in energy storage power plants.

articleTitle: Compliant Assembly of Electrical Connector Based on Contact Search and Force Control with Robotics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: The assembly of electrical connectors by space robots is one of the important requirements for in-orbit service. In this paper, aiming at the difficulty of fine assembly of electrical connectors with multi-point coupling contact under the vision-limited conditions, an adaptive assembly method of circular electrical connectors with contact search and robotic force control based on “two-point contact-flexible sliding-attitude correction-alignment and insertion” is proposed. By establishing a dynamic model based on contact and collision, and introducing a force/torque-position hybrid impedance control algorithm, the high reliability assembly of the circular electrical connector is realized by experimental verification, which provides support for the maintenance of the spacecraft.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Voltage Restoration in Islanded Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: Virtual impedance is widely used in microgrid to decouple active and reactive power control. To mitigate the virtual-impedance-induced voltage deviation, this paper investigates an event-triggered voltage restoration control scheme. The virtual-impedance-induced voltage drop is deduced and expressed in reactive power. Then voltage restoration is formulated as a distributed optimization problem. Event-triggering technique is employed to reduce communication load. By solving the distributed optimization problem, average voltage restoration and accurate reactive power sharing can be achieved simultaneously. Simulation shows that the proposed method is effective.

articleTitle: Parametric Study of Inlet Temperature and Flow Rate for Cascade Hydrogen Refueling from Liquid Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: Since the volumetric hydrogen storage density of low-temperature LHS is much higher than that of high-pressure gaseous hydrogen storage, the liquid hydrogen storage (LHS) type hydrogen refueling station has a greater advantage in hydrogen storage compared with the high-pressure gaseous hydrogen storage type hydrogen refueling station, which is more in line with the development trend of the hydrogen fuel cell vehicles. This paper focuses on the LHS-type cascade refueling and establishes a zero-dimensional lumped parameter model for the LHS-type cascade refueling system by using the MATLAB/Simulink platform, and carries out a parametric study on the refueling process of the vehicle-mounted hydrogen storage tanks based on the model, and analyzes and compares the effects of different inlet flow rates and inlet temperatures on the refueling effect.

articleTitle: Robust Federated Learning with Valid Gradient Direction for Cloud-Edge-End Collaboration in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: With the advancement of carbon emissions reduction initiatives, there is a rapid increase in the current demand for electrical power, which necessitates a more efficient and reliable grid to meet this demand. Consequently, smart grids are proposed to address these new challenges. At the same time, to protect user privacy during big data analysis, smart grids introduce the federated learning algorithm involving three types of devices: cloud, edge, and end devices. However, previous federated learning algorithms based on cloud-edge-end collaboration typically do not assess whether user data contains noise, which leads to insufficient robustness of the models. To address this issue, we propose a new Robust Federated Learning (RoFed) method for end-device parameters selection based on the gradient directions of parameters. RoFed can filter out abnormal end devices based on the angle between gradient directions of each device and the average gradient direction per round. This filtering can prevent the end devices trained with noisy data from participating in the aggregation of parameters on the cloud device. Experiments on 13 real-world electric power data classification datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of RoFed.

articleTitle: A Changepoints and Phased Trends Detection Method for Dam Deformation Monitoring Sequence Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: The changepoints detection, phased trend identification and deformation cause analysis of dam deformation monitoring sequences help to deepen the understanding of the evolution of dam deformation in different time scales, which is of great significance for dam safety operation and management. We designed the process for analyzing dam deformation monitoring data from variational mode decomposition, changepoints detection, segmental trend analysis to correlation analysis, and used this process to analyze the ideal time series simulation signal, the standard test Bumps simulation signal, and inverse plummet deformation monitoring data of the Datengxia Dam from May 2022 to May 2024 respectively. The variational mode decomposition (VMD) method is used to decompose the dam deformation monitoring sequence to the normal dam deformation component(U1), environmental impact component (U2), and other noise influence subitems U3 and U4 are obtained, which effectively avoids the interference of the other noise terms on the changepoints detection and trend identification. On this basis, improved Bayesian block (BBLOCKS) algorithm is used to detect changepoints in component U1, and U1 is divided into sub-segments with stable trends. Then, Mann-Kendal trend analysis (MK) and innovative trend analysis (ITA) methods are used respectively to identify the trend of each sub-segment, which helps to analyze the reasons for the changes in each sub-segment individually. Finally, correlation analysis was done between the U2 subseries and the environmental impacting factors such as temperature, water level and osmotic pressure, and the correlation coefficient between the U2 subseries and temperature = 0.96, which has the highest correlation, and is the main cause of the U2 subseries, indicating that the temperature change has a sustained effect on the deformation of the dam. Examples show that the dam data analysis process recommended of variational modal decomposition, changepoints detection, segmental trend analysis, and correlation analysis of environmental impact factors effectively decomposes the data into various sub components and sub-segments, which plays an important role in trend analysis and cause analysis of deformation.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Voice Interaction System Based on Intent Recognition and Large Model Technology in the Context of Electrical Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: With the advancement of large language models, the importance of optimizing question-answering systems using these models has become increasingly prominent. To achieve efficient and accurate electrical equipment inspection in the context of electrical safety checks, we propose an intelligent voice interaction system based on intent recognition and large model technology. This system integrates domain knowledge such as the electrical inspection process and conventional electrical knowledge base into the dialogue system, uses the BERT-BiLSTM model to classify user intents, and then adopts different dialogue generation strategies according to different intents, thereby solving the problem that large language models cannot answer knowledge in the specific field of electrical safety inspection. Finally, through the implementation of the interaction system in the context of electrical inspection, we verified the feasibility of this method.

articleTitle: Study on the Acoustic Emission Characteristics and Fracture of Coal Samples with Different Bedding under Brazilian Splitting Test
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: To investigate the crack and acoustic emission characteristics of coal sample with diverse bedding angles under Brazilian fracturing test, the Brazilian fracturing tests with diverse bedding angles of 0°, 30°, 45° and 60° were conducted, and the evolution regular pattern of acoustic emission signals were monitored in real time, and then the fracture features of coal sample with diverse bedding angles were contrasted and studied. The experimental results indicated that the maximum peak load is 2.07 kN when the bedding angle is 0°, and the minimum peak load is 0.51 kN when the bedding angle is 45°. The tensile strength of coal samples varied a U-shaped tendency with increasing bedding angle. During the initial phase of loading, the acoustic emission count is very small, but it increases to some extent in the middle stage of loading. By the late stage of loading, the damage level of the coal samples with bedding angles of 0° and 45° is the greatest, and the acoustic emission count exceeds 6,000 times. Combined with the analysis of acoustic emission RA-AF characteristics, it is shown that the failure of coal sample with diverse angles of bedding is not a single failure, but a complex failure of tension and shear, in which tensile failure is the primary failure form. This study provides some guidance for analyzing fracture characteristics in diverse bedding directions and forming complex fracture networks in hydraulic fracturing.

articleTitle: Ultra-Short-Term Wind Power Prediction Based on ICEEMDAN-Nons-Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: The electric power system with a high proportion of renewable energy integration is confronted with a series of problems such as intermittency, volatility and uncertainty, which poses great challenges to its stable operation. Therefore, enhancing the accuracy of wind power prediction holds key significance for power system scheduling. To address this issue, a hybrid model for ultra-short-term wind power prediction is put forward: ICEEMDAN-Nons-Transformer. Firstly, the initial wind power data is decomposed into multiple Intrinsic Mode Function (IMF) components using an Improved Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (ICEEMDAN) algorithm. Then, Nons-Transformer algorithm is used for model training and prediction of each component obtained from ICEEMDAN decomposition. Ultimately, the prediction results of each IMF components are reconstructed to acquire the eventual prediction results and carry out experimental analysis. The evaluation index results show that ICEEMDAN-Nons-Transformer model is superior to the mentioned single reference model and hybrid model, and can effectively process time series data, with certain effectiveness and potential use value.

articleTitle: An Improved Time Series Temperature Prediction Algorithm Based on Kalman Filter and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: Climate change is critical for social and economic development, and it also affects human production and life. Studies have shown that the temperature is rising at a rate of 0.2 degrees Celsius per decade, and rising temperatures are also affecting human health. Therefore, it is urgent to improve the accuracy of temperature forecasts. Studies on literature about temperature prediction using traditional time series method models and deep learning have been relatively standard in the existing literature. Still, only some studies combine methods from different fields and apply them to combined models. Therefore, it is difficult to deal with the nonlinear factors in temperature prediction, and its prediction accuracy will decrease when factors such as wind and air pressure change abruptly. Therefore, we used the Kalman filter to enhance the conventional autoregressive approach by integrating it with other factors, alongside both long-term and short-term memory networks, aiming to refine and improve the accuracy of the temperature forecasts. The experimental results show that although the prediction results of this paper are slightly worse than other models in some cities, the overall performance of this model is better than other models, and it can achieve more accurate temperature prediction.

articleTitle: Prediction of Ultra-Short-Term Wind Power Based on VMD-Transformer-SSA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: With the integration of a high proportion of renewable energy sources into power systems, the issues such as the peak load problem, supply and demand imbalance, and integration problem brought about by the probabilistic and variable nature of wind power generation have once again become the focus of attention. Ultimately, enhancing the accuracy of wind power prediction holds significant meaning for improving the stability of renewable energy systems. In addressing this issue, a new framework has been presented that will enhance the accuracy of short-term wind energy forecasting - VMD-Transformer-SSA. Firstly, the existing wind power generation data is separated into the components of internal mode functions within multiple functions. Subsequently, we leverage the quantity of efficiency optimizations achieved and the learning rate dynamics of the transformers within the intricate deep neural system. This approach enables us to identify and select the optimal parameters that are harmonious with the transformer model's architecture and requirements, thereby enhancing its performance and effectiveness. By doing so, we ensure that the model is optimally configured to leverage the advancements in efficiency and learning capabilities. Next, models are established and predictions are made for each IMF component obtained from the VMD decomposition. Ultimately, the individual predictions for each constituent component are meticulously reassembled to yield a comprehensive and refined final forecast. The empirical evaluation, through simulations, underscores the efficacy of the VMD-Transformer-SSA framework in adeptly managing the intricacies of time series data and accurately predicting short-term wind power generation. This performance exceeds that of benchmark models, demonstrating the framework's superiority in harnessing the unique strengths of its constituent algorithms to deliver superior predictive capabilities.

articleTitle: Research on Lithium Battery Fire Suppression Strategy Based on LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: Aiming at the phenomenon that there is the risk of thermal runaway and easy to cause fire and explosion in the abnormal condition of lithium battery storage module, this paper analyzes the thermal runaway and combustion characteristics of lithium battery, and chooses liquid nitrogen as fire extinguishing agent, a method for predicting the thermal loss of control of lithium battery based on LSTM (Long Short Term Memory) neural network was proposed. According to the predicted results, the injection rate of extinguishing agent and exhaust fan rate were controlled, and the fire extinguishing operation was carried out regularly. The simulation results show that this method can effectively restrain the thermal runaway of the lithium battery and prevent the explosion, so as to completely control the fire.

articleTitle: Modeling of Altitude Ground Test Facility Intake Systems and Temperature-Pressure Synchronized Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: High-altitude simulation testing on altitude ground test facility is one of the most effective ways to verify the high-altitude performance of aero-engine. Accurately simulating the intake/exhaust temperature and pressure conditions of aero-engine at high altitude environment is a key part of the high-altitude simulation test. During the acceleration and deceleration test of aero-engine, the rapid change of demand flow affects the pressure simulation of the altitude ground test facility intake system, thereby affecting the accuracy of the aero-engine high-altitude test results. By analyzing the multi-loop temperature and pressure coupling characteristics of the intake system, GT-SUITE and Simulink are used to jointly establish an accurate intake system model, and a PI controller parameters are optimized based on the whale optimization algorithm to achieve synchronous adjustment of the temperature and pressure of the intake system, thereby achieving the intake system pressure quickly followed control during the engine acceleration/deceleration test.

Author Keywords: altitude ground test facility intake system

articleTitle: Research on the Environmental Impact of Photovoltaic Cell Output Based on Ideal Solar Radiation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: As an important part of the renewable energy system, photovoltaic power generation has received more and more attention and application. As a semiconductor component of photoelectric conversion, photovoltaic cell's power generation and battery life are significantly affected by temperature. In order to explore the change of output power caused by the environmental impact of photovoltaic cells, the energy control equation of photovoltaic panels was established by combining the ideal sunny day solar radiation model, and the existing experimental data were used to verify the reliability of the model. The influence law of latitude, altitude, wind speed and temperature on the temperature and output power of photovoltaic cells was mainly studied. The results show that temperature, altitude and wind speed have significant effects on the power thermal attenuation of photovoltaic cells. The influence of latitude is related to the date, and the area with the largest thermal attenuation of photovoltaic cell power appears in the region of 22° to 32° north latitude on the summer solstice. The research in this paper provides a theoretical basis for the design of cooling methods for photovoltaic cells.

articleTitle: Effect of Tunnel LED Skylight Illumination on Drivers’ Eye Movements and Physiological Responses
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: This study analyzes the dynamic change of driver's visual attention and physiological reaction with a real vehicle test. Eye movements including fixation and pupil regulation, heart rates, skin conductance, and other physiological indicators were recorded when driving through different lighting schemes of the Taihu Tunnel on the Su-xiChang South Freeway. The results suggest that landscape lighting amplifies drivers’ focus on the broader driving view, yet it may also affect pupil dilation. These findings lay the groundwork for choosing the final lighting scheme, which is crucial for improving traffic safety and refining driving experience.

articleTitle: Oxygen Removal from Coal Mine Methane by Vacuum Pressure Swing Adsorption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: The aim of this study was to develop a safe, efficient and environmentally friendly method for the treatment of coal mine methane (CMM) in order to achieve its efficient utilisation as an energy source while reducing the safety risks and environmental issues associated with it. Oxygen removal from a model CMM, which contained about 37 % CH4 and the balance air, was carried out by vacuum pressure swing adsorption (VPSA). Two commercial carbon molecular sieves, CMS1 and CMS2, were used as adsorbents, in which CMS1 has higher selectivities of O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>. To ensure the safety of the oxygen removal process, a rinse step with N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as rinse gas followed by the adsorption step was introduced. With the rinse step, the oxygen could be safely and effectively separated from CMM. Combining the advantages of both CMS1 and CMS2, a layered VPSA was proposed. Under the operating condition of the feedstock gas flow rate 750 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/min, the adsorption time 120 s, the rinse time 40 s and the rinse pressure 0.43 MPa (abs.), a product gas with over 50 % CH4 and less than 0.5 % O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, an off-gas with CH4 below 3 %, and a CH4 recovery of higher than 95 % were obtained. The results not only meet the objectives of this study, but also provide a viable technological solution for the safe utilisation of CMM and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning Algorithms for Enhanced Smart Grid Control and Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth exploration of machine learning (ML) applications in smart grids, focusing on six key areas: demand forecasting, energy management, microgrid control, power electronic control, fault detection, and predictive maintenance. It examines the transformative impact of ML in enhancing smart grid efficiency, reliability, and functionality, drawing on current research and case studies. The study delves into the challenges of data management and privacy, scalability issues, and the future trends of ML in smart grids. The findings highlight ML's crucial role in optimizing operations, managing complex power systems, and integrating renewable energy sources, emphasizing the need for scalable and adaptable algorithms. The paper concludes by discussing potential future developments in ML applications for smart grids, including advanced predictive analytics and improved resilience against natural and cyber threats, underscoring the importance of continuous innovation in the energy sector.

articleTitle: Decoupling Control of Geometrical Consistency for Formation UAVs Based on Node Importance Identification of Temporal Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: To address the issue of geometric consistency in the formation of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) during flight, from the perspective of formation control, an identification method for the core nodes of the temporal network is introduced to analyze and evaluate the geometric position error of the UAV formation. A decoupling controller is designed to improve the geometric consistency of the UAV formation. During the design process, the UAVs' dynamics model is established and a Leader-Follower formation controller is designed based on LMI and virtual Leader. The node importance identification of the UAV formation is determined by constructing a time series network according to the similarity based super adjacency matrix (SSAM) of nodes, and the controller is improved in the light of the results of node importance recognition. In the simulation process, the tracking effect of the dual aircraft formation was first verified and analyzed. Then, taking the 6-aircraft formation as an example, the relationship between node importance and geometric consistency was analyzed, and the controller was improved. The simulation results showed that the improved controller, taking into account the factors affecting node importance, can improve the geometric consistency of the formation, providing meaningful reference value for the study of maintaining and consistency control of Formation organization and formation maintenance formations.

articleTitle: Computational Analysis on Jump Height of Overhead Transmission Lines After Uneven Ice Shedding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: The jump height of overhead transmission lines after uneven de-icing is of great significance to the planning of conductor head gap. ANSYS software was used to study the dynamic responses of transmission lines with various structural parameters, such as the number of spans, span length, elevation difference, ice thickness, wind speed, and length of suspension insulator strings, following ice shedding at various rates. By proposing the concepts of conversion span length, isolated span correction coefficient, and uneven ice-shedding jump height coefficient, a calculating method of jump height of single span and multiple span under uniform and non-uniform ice load was found. Furthermore, a comparison was conducted between the numerical calculation method and the finite element model (FEM). The results show that uneven ice shedding jumps higher than uniform ice shedding under the same ice-shedding load in one span, and the relative error of the proposed calculation formula for uneven ice-shedding jump height is within 13.2%, which meets the accuracy requirements in the design of phase to phase or interphase safety gap.

articleTitle: Some Optimal Ternary Linear Complementary Dual Codes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes introduced by Massey are the codes whose intersections with their dual codes are trivial. It can help to improve the security of the information processed by sensitive devices, especially against side-channel attacks (SCA) and fault invasive attacks. In this paper, by construction of puncturing, shortening and combination codes, many good ternary LCD codes are presented. Some of optimal LCD codes are constructed by quasi-cyclic codes. In addition, the values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{LCD}(n,k)$</tex> for length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\leq 26$</tex> are given. Many of these ternary LCD codes given in this paper are optimal which are saturating the lower or upper bound of Grassl's codetable and some of them are near-optimal.

articleTitle: Efficiency Electrical Power Edge-end Computing with Patch-based Low-rank Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: The development of communication technology has made the need to build more reliable and efficient smart power grid systems imminent. The emergence of edge computing has significantly alleviated the pressure of data transmission in systems, enhancing the reliability and stability of cloud-edge based smart grid systems. However, the deep algorithms on which current Edge Computing platforms rely increase the overall computation time consumption and memory consumption of the whole system, which is inconsistent with the responsiveness and reliability requirements of smart power grid system services. Therefore, in this paper, we propose Patch-based Low-rank Transformer (PLT) that balances accuracy and efficiency, which can greatly alleviate the computation time consumption and memory consumption of Edge Computing platforms. Specifically, we cut the original electric power time series into subsequence-level patches to ensure the accuracy of the model for long and short-term sequential dependencies learning. Then, we introduce a low-rank attention mechanism to reduce the computational consumption of the model, and design a simple but efficient knowledge distillation module that transferring knowledge from the Transformer-based model to a lightweight MLP to speed up the computation of the model at inference phrase. Extensive experiments on 11 public datasets (10 UCR and 1 cluster-trace-v2018 released by Alibaba Cloud) and 13 collected electric power time series datasets show that the proposed PLT outperforms baseline models and reaches the design purpose.

articleTitle: An Inference Optimization Method for Distribution Network Planning Projects Based on ANFIS Historical Preferences
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: The requirement for precise investment requires proactive distribution network planning project optimization when the scale of investment is limited. However, the commonly used multi-dimensional evaluation index system of planning projects may not be able to meet the needs of different distribution networks due to the influence of experts' tendencies, and the historical experience of distribution network planning in the region cannot be reflected. The historical planning project has gone through the decision-making process of experts from various departments of the distribution network in the region, and its project selection implies expert knowledge, and on this basis, a distribution network planning project optimization model is proposed based on the selection preference of the historical distribution network planning project for training. First, combining the theory of the Life Cycle Cost (LCC) to establish an indicator system for the investment benefit evaluation of the distribution network. Then, for the project evaluation system that has been established, a fuzzy inference mechanism based on an Adaptive Network-based Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) is used to learn the historical preferences of planning projects. This transforms the historical experience of planners into weight adjustments for the objective evaluation of distribution network projects. Finally, the model is used to validate a distribution network planning project in a certain urban power supply bureau through a case study. The validation confirms the accuracy and feasibility of the proposed model, providing reasonable guidance for enhancing the precision of investments in distribution network assets.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches to Improve Fault Location and Diagnosis in Smart Grids: Current Trends and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: This review paper explores the use of machine learning (ML) in enhancing fault location and diagnosis within smart grids. It highlights the transition from traditional electricity distribution to advanced systems leveraging real-time data and communication networks. The paper examines various ML algorithms, such as neural networks, decision trees, and support vector machines, and their application in accurately detecting, locating, and diagnosing grid faults. It underscores the significance of ML in improving grid reliability and efficiency, particularly in integrating intermittent renewable energy sources. The review also discusses challenges related to data quality, model interpretability, and system integration, offering insights into overcoming these obstacles. Additionally, it looks at future directions for ML in smart grids, considering ongoing technological advancements. The paper concludes with strategic recommendations for researchers and practitioners in the field, emphasizing the role of ML in driving a more sustainable, efficient, and reliable energy future.

articleTitle: Real-Time Monitoring and Verification Analysis of Calcium-Sulfur Molar Ratio in Wet Desulfurization of Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: In limestone-gypsum wet desulfurization system, calcium sulfur mole ratio (hereinafter referred to as calcium sulfur ratio) is one of the main economic indicators, but also one of the performance indicators of flue gas desulfurization system. In this paper, a mathematical model of the calcium-sulfur ratio index of the wet desulphurization system of a coal-fired power plant is established. Based on the big data related to the operation of the wet desulphurization system of a 300 MW unit, the real-time operation of the calcium-sulfur ratio index is obtained. The influencing factors on the calcium-sulfur ratio are further analyzed, and the results of the calcium-sulfur ratio are revised. At the same time, a method to modify the ratio of calcium to sulfur in desulphurization system under different load operation is proposed. The error is less than 0.5 % when comparing the modified Ca/S ratio with the Ca/S ratio measured by the gypsum slurry composition analysis method, which indicates that the Ca/S ratio determination method based on the operation big data is accurate and reliable, and provides a convenient new method for real-time Ca/S ratio determination in the wet desulfurization system of coal-fired power plant.

articleTitle: Research on Energy Supply & Demand Balance Under New Energy System in China Based on the CEMS Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: Building a new energy system is an important way for China to achieve its “dual carbon” goals. Accurately grasping the positioning and supply-demand balance of various energy varieties in the new energy system is of great significance for ensuring energy supply and green low-carbon transformation. Based on the CEMS model, the energy and electricity demand in three different scenarios (baseline scenario, enhanced energy-saving scenario, and accelerated green transformation scenario) were analyzed and predicted, and energy flow charts for 2030 and 2060 were drawn to reflect the supply-demand relationship of different energy varieties. The research results indicate that under the new energy system, the proportion of fossil fuels will continue to decrease, but they will still play a key role in supporting, regulating the system, and utilizing raw materials for a long time. The proportion of new energy is rapidly increasing and it will become the largest energy source between 2040 and 2045. Compared to the baseline scenario, the energy demand under the strengthened energysaving scenario has decreased, in which carbon peak is achieved two years earlier. In the scenario of accelerating green transformation, the proportion of non-fossil fuels is higher, energy demand has increased, and carbon peak is achieved one year earlier.

articleTitle: Research on the Method for Determining the Equivalent Amount of Explosive for Group Hole Simultaneous Blasting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: Due to the delay error of the novel detonator, the blasting holes are not initiated at their nominal delay time, the seismic wave at the measuring point overlaps with the staggered peak, and the peak value of blasting peak vibration velocity changes. Therefore, there is doubt about the value of an equivalent charge weight per delay when predicting blasting peak vibration velocity in engineering. A field monitoring test of the vibration of simultaneous blasting detonator based on a non-electrical detonator was designed and carried out. A peak vibration velocity calculation model for the explosive for group hole simultaneous blasting was constructed, and the influence mechanism of detonator delay error on the equivalent charge weight per delay of group hole blasting was explored. On this basis, the number of holes scaling index m and the value method of the equivalent amount of explosive for group hole simultaneous blasting was innovatively introduced. The results show that under the same total charge, the equivalent amount of explosive is smaller than the nominal amount of explosive. The scaling index M can effectively reduce the error between the predicted value and the measured value of blasting peak vibration velocity, and it is feasible to calculate the equivalent amount of explosive of simultaneous blasting. The research results can provide a theoretical basis for the prediction and control of the peak vibration velocity of electronic detonator delayed blasting in the short millisecond case.

articleTitle: Research on Vertical Sharing and Penetration Technology of Smart Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: In this paper, aiming at the problems such as the difficulty of expanding the breadth and depth of substation centralized monitoring, the low degree of business collaboration and data sharing between the main and sub-stations, and the poor relevance of the main and auxiliary business in the substation, the vertical data sharing and business collaboration between the main and sub-stations are supported through the construction of equipment model fusion method, service interaction mechanism and data resource pool architecture. Support holographic panoramic monitoring such as collaborative monitoring, collaborative early warning, collaborative operation and maintenance of remote master station.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of DESS Considering Power Variations and Data Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Energy and Electrical Engineering (EEE)
abstract: The reliability of battery containers is closely related to the multidimensional battery variables and power conversion system (PCS) real-time power. However, the research on batteries and PCS remains insufficient. Digital energy storage systems (DESS) integrates devices such as battery energy exchange switches, battery energy concentrators, battery energy adapters, battery cluster (BC), PCS, and battery energy network cards, but their reliability presents a complex challenge to resolve. This paper proposes a novel approach for assessing the reliability of DESS by considering PCS power variations and BC data reconstructions. Using a multi-state probability analysis, a unified fault rate calculation model for PCS components is established based on magnitude power and intensity fluctuation. Additionally, this study also introduces Bi-LSTM to calculate BC data reconstruction for DESS's BC and PCS presents a comprehensive reliability assessment model for the entire system. This model provides a more accurate reflection of the impact of power variations and data reconstructions on DESS's comprehensive reliability.
